learningOutcomes: Distinguish between standardized exchange-traded futures and customized Over-the-Counter (OTC) forward contracts, and compare their global market scale [fact-01, fact-02, fact-07].
Calculate terminal payoffs for long and short forward/futures positions and evaluate CME Corn futures contract specifications [fact-03, fact-09].
Execute corporate foreign exchange forward hedging calculations using two-sided USD/GBP quotes [fact-08].
Quantify how balance-sheet leverage dictates capital equity wipeout thresholds and analyze Lehman Brothers' 2008 bankruptcy [fact-04, fact-05].
Explain the systemic risk domino effect and post-2008 OTC regulatory reforms including Central Counterparties [fact-06].

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Futures use daily mark-to-market clearing house settlement that eliminates bilateral credit risk, whereas traditional forwards settle at maturity and carry direct counterparty credit risk [fact-01, fact-02].

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Market-makers quote two-sided Bid and Offer rates; importers buy at the higher Offer rate while exporters sell at the lower Bid rate [fact-08].

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: At a 31:1 leverage ratio, Lehman's equity buffer was only 3.23% (1 / 31), meaning a tiny 3% to 4% asset decline wiped out 100% of its equity capital [fact-04].

activeRecallQuiz.scenario: On May 13, 2015, 3-month USD/GBP forwards are quoted at 1.5736 Bid / 1.5742 Offer. ImportCo hedges a £10 million payable. Simultaneously, an investment bank operates at a 31:1 leverage ratio.
activeRecallQuiz.question: What USD payment does ImportCo lock in, and what asset decline percentage wipes out 100% of the bank's equity?
activeRecallQuiz.correctAnswer: Correctly identifying the downside risk and margin constraints.
activeRecallQuiz.explanation: ImportCo pays the 3-month forward Offer rate of $1.5742/£, resulting in £10,000,000 × $1.5742 = $15,742,000 [fact-08]. For the bank at 31:1 leverage, Equity % = 1 / 31 ≈ 3.23%, so a 3% to 4% asset drop wipes out 100% of equity [fact-04].

coreTakeaways: Derivatives transfer price risk across two distinct markets: standardized exchange futures ($65T) and customized bilateral OTC contracts ($630T notional) [fact-01, fact-02, fact-07, fact-09].
Forward and futures contracts have symmetric linear payoffs (S_T - K for long; K - S_T for short) and support precise corporate FX hedging using Bid and Offer quotes [fact-03, fact-08].
Extreme leverage (31:1 at Lehman Brothers) and opaque OTC entanglements create systemic domino risk, mitigated post-2008 by SEFs, CCP clearing, and CSA margins [fact-04, fact-05, fact-06].
